segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And Jesus answered and spake unto them again by parables, and said,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was teaching in the temple, and the men who were hunting for a way to arrest him were standing right in front of him. So he told them a story: about a king, a wedding, and an invitation that almost nobody took.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A king was giving a wedding feast for his son. The oxen were prepared, the tables were loaded, the hall was full of light. And the guests had been invited long before. They had already said they would come.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So when the day arrived, the king sent his servants to go and bring them in.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they would not come. Not one of them. They had said yes, and now, with everything ready and waiting, they simply would not walk over.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They all had something else. A field to go look at. A shop to keep. The king's own guests looked at his son's wedding and decided they had better things to do.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And some of them did worse. They turned on the servants who came to invite them. It was the kind of insult a kingdom does not survive, and that city did not survive it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the feast was still ready. The food was still hot. And a hall built for a wedding was standing empty. So the king made a decision.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy. Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Out to the roads. Not the guest list. The roads. Whoever happened to be out there. The day laborers, the beggars, the people nobody ever puts on a list.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They brought in everyone they could find. The story does not clean it up. It says both the bad and the good, and the wedding hall filled right up.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And here is the part almost everyone misses. Nobody dragged in off the street owned wedding clothes. At a king's feast, the clean festival robe was the king's to give, handed to every guest at the door. Every person in that hall was wearing something the king had put on them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the king came in to meet his guests. And he found one man still in his own dusty road clothes. Not because he was too poor. Everyone there was too poor. Because he had been handed a robe at the door, and had said no to it.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Friend. That is what the king called him. Not intruder. Not thief. Friend, and a question, and every chance in the world to answer. And the man had nothing to say.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He had come to the feast and refused the one thing that made him a guest. So he ended up where he had chosen to be. Back outside, in the dark, away from a light that had been standing wide open for him.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The men listening knew exactly who the story was about. They were the invited guests, the ones who had said yes for a lifetime and would not come when the King actually arrived. But do not miss what the story is really doing.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: For many are called, but few are chosen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Everyone is invited. That is the whole world. The ones who end up at the table are simply the ones who came, and who let the King put the clean clothes on them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You do not have to make yourself presentable first. Nobody in that hall could have, and neither can you. The invitation is free, the door is open, and the clean clothes are already bought and folded and waiting inside. All you have to do is come in, and let him dress you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The King fills his hall with people straight off the road, and hands each one clean clothes at the door. What has he been holding out for you to put on, that you keep walking past?
